# Content-default fixtures

These are three image fixtures for the D2 classifier, not a general accuracy corpus.

| Fixture | Source | Expected suggestion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `screenshot.bmp` | Existing local `e2e/fixtures/ocr-corpus/clean-screenshot.png`, generated by `scripts/generate-ocr-corpus.mjs` | Screenshot / app, Original |
| `phone-page.bmp` | `phone-page.jpg`, an actual photographed book page | Document, Adaptive document |
| `terminal.bmp` | Existing local `e2e/fixtures/ocr-corpus/code-terminal.png`, generated by `scripts/generate-ocr-corpus.mjs` | Screenshot / app, Original |

The original phone photograph is Matt Zucker's `boston_cooking_a.jpg` from
[page_dewarp](https://github.com/mzucker/page_dewarp/blob/master/example_input/boston_cooking_a.jpg),
retrieved 17 September 2026. The EXIF Make/Model is Apple / iPhone 6.
SHA-256: `b7e3aac880412b7967c49b0b3271fb58a333a614fab0abf58e2bd137de3482f3`.
The upstream MIT licence is included in `LICENSE-page-dewarp.txt`.
The author's [project description](https://mzucker.github.io/2016/08/15/page-dewarping.html)
identifies the example as a photograph of a curled page. This fixture is for tests
only and is not shipped as a public sample or imported into the application.

BMPs contain the production-sized thumbnails, at most 192 pixels on either side,
as uncompressed top-down 32-bit pixels. Unit tests decode these without a native
canvas or extra dependency. `node scripts/measure-content-defaults.mjs` verifies
that Chromium recreates the same pixels from the original images and records
browser timings. Use `--refresh-fixtures`
only to deliberately regenerate them. Tests and timing runs need no network access.
